items.stem: Explain why a person carrying a heavy bag horizontally at constant speed does no work on the bag against gravity.
items.answer: The force supporting the bag is vertical and the displacement is horizontal, so the angle is 90° and the work done, Fd cos 90°, is zero.
items.markingKey: B1 force perpendicular to displacement; B1 cos 90° = 0 [2]

items.stem: A box of mass 10 kg is pulled 5 m across rough horizontal ground (μ = 0.1) by a force of 40 N at 50° above the horizontal. Lina uses R = 100 N to find the work done against friction. Explain the error and find the correct value.
items.answer: The pull has an upward component, so R = 100 − 40 sin 50° = 69.4 N; work against friction = μRd = 34.7 J.
items.markingKey: B1 R reduced by the vertical component; B1 correct work [2]

items.stem: Explain why the change in gravitational potential energy of a particle moving along a slope depends only on its change in height.
items.answer: Gravity acts vertically, so only the vertical displacement contributes to the work done by the weight; mgh depends on the vertical height change, not the path.
items.markingKey: B1 weight acts vertically; B1 only vertical displacement matters [2]

items.stem: Explain why the kinetic energy of a 10 kg particle moving at 2 m s⁻¹ is the same whether it moves left or right, while its momentum is not.
items.answer: KE = (1/2)mv² depends on v², so the sign of v does not matter (20 J); momentum mv is a vector and changes sign (±20 N s).
items.markingKey: B1 KE scalar using v²; B1 momentum vector [2]

items.stem: When is mechanical energy (KE + GPE) conserved?
options: when no work is done by forces other than weight
only when the speed is constant
items.answer: when no work is done by forces other than weight
items.markingKey: e.g. smooth surfaces and no air resistance.

items.stem: Explain why energy methods can find the speed of a particle at the bottom of a smooth curved slope when suvat cannot.
items.answer: On a curved slope the acceleration is not constant, so suvat does not apply; but with no friction the total mechanical energy is conserved, so the speed follows from the height lost.
items.markingKey: B1 acceleration varies; B1 energy depends only on height [2]

items.stem: Felix says a 10 kg ball and a 20 kg ball released from rest at the same height of 10 m will reach the ground with different speeds. Use energy to explain why this is wrong (ignore air resistance).
items.answer: mgh = (1/2)mv² gives v = √(2gh) = 14.1 m s⁻¹; m cancels.
items.markingKey: M1 energy equation; A1 m cancels [2]

items.stem: A sledge of mass 5 kg is pulled 4 m across rough horizontal snow by a rope inclined at 50° above the horizontal with tension 10 N. The coefficient of friction is 0.6. (a) Find the work done by the tension. (b) Find the work done against friction. (c) State the work done by the weight and by the normal reaction, giving a reason.
items.answer: (a) 25.7 J (b) 102 J (c) 0 J for each: both are perpendicular to the motion
items.markingKey: (a) M1 Fd cos θ; A1 value [2] (b) M1 μRd; A1 value [2] (c) B1 zero with reason [1]

items.stem: Find the kinetic energy of a particle of mass 800 kg moving at 6 m s⁻¹.
items.markingKey: KE = (1/2)mv².

items.stem: The speed of a 4 kg particle changes from 6 m s⁻¹ to 3 m s⁻¹. Grace finds the change in kinetic energy as (1/2) × 4 × (3 − 6)² = 18 J. Explain the error and correct it.
items.markingKey: B1 difference of squares, not square of difference; B1 correct value [2]

items.stem: Omar calculates the kinetic energy of a 10 kg particle moving at 10 m s⁻¹ as 1000 J. Explain the error.
items.answer: KE = (1/2)mv² = 500 J; the factor 1/2 is missing.
items.markingKey: B1 factor 1/2; B1 correct value [2]

items.stem: A skier of mass 50 kg descends a slope inclined at 35°, losing 10 m in height. Her speed increases from 4 m s⁻¹ to 8 m s⁻¹. (a) Find the distance travelled along the slope. (b) Find the loss in gravitational potential energy. (c) Hence find the work done against resistance.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 h/sin α [1] (b) B1 mgh [1] (c) M1 difference; A1 value [2]

items.stem: A skier of mass 80 kg descends a slope inclined at 20°, losing 20 m in height. Her speed increases from 2 m s⁻¹ to 8 m s⁻¹. (a) Find the distance travelled along the slope. (b) Find the loss in gravitational potential energy. (c) Find the gain in kinetic energy. (d) Hence find the work done against resistance.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 h/sin α [1] (b) B1 mgh [1] (c) M1 (1/2)m(v² − u²); A1 value [2] (d) M1 difference; A1 value [2]

items.stem: A ball is thrown vertically upwards at 14.1 m s⁻¹. Using energy, find the greatest height it reaches.
items.markingKey: mgh = (1/2)mu².

items.stem: A block slides down a rough slope of vertical height 20 m. Yusuf finds its speed at the bottom using (1/2)mv² = mgh. Explain why this overestimates the speed.
items.answer: On a rough slope friction does work against the motion, so some of the GPE is converted to heat; the KE gained is less than mgh.
items.markingKey: B1 friction does work; B1 KE less than mgh [2]

items.stem: Two smooth slides start at the same height 20 m above the ground, one straight and one curved. Explain why a child starting from rest reaches the bottom of each with the same speed.
items.answer: Mechanical energy is conserved on smooth slides; the speed depends only on the height lost: v = √(2gh) = 20.0 m s⁻¹ for both.
items.markingKey: B1 conservation of energy; B1 independent of path [2]

items.stem: A particle is projected down a smooth curved track with speed 4 m s⁻¹ from a point 20 m above the bottom. Find its speed at the bottom.
items.markingKey: M1 KE + PE conserved; A1 speed [2]

items.stem: A particle slides along a smooth track. At A, its speed is 10 m s⁻¹; B is 2 m higher than A. Find the speed of the particle at B.
items.markingKey: M1 energy equation; A1 speed [2]

items.stem: A particle of mass 20 kg moves along a smooth track. It starts at A, 20 m above the ground, with speed 3 m s⁻¹. B is a point on the track 6 m above the ground and C is at ground level. (a) Find the speed of the particle at B. (b) Find the speed of the particle at C. (c) State one modelling assumption you have made.
items.answer: (a) 17.0 m s⁻¹ (b) 20.2 m s⁻¹ (c) the track is smooth (no friction) and air resistance is ignored
items.markingKey: (a) B1 speed [1] (b) M1 energy; A1 speed [2] (c) B1 [1]
